svg.title: Level 1 Standard: an exploratory analysis
svg.desc: Level 1 Standard: an exploratory analysis. Stages run across and lanes run down. Exploratory analysis, which NHSBSA's Analytical Assurance Decision Tool gives as a worked example of impact 1. Drawn here at Level 1 Standard, which is where impact 1 lands at low to high likelihood. The route this playbook sets out for work of that kind, not a record of a particular piece of work. Stages, left to right: Engagement and scoping, Design, Analysis, Delivery and sign-off and Review. Commissioner. Owns the question and the resource. Engagement and scoping: State the decision the analysis informs, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. Score the impact with the analyst. Design: Make sure there is time for the colleague check. No design gate is required at this level. Analysis: Stay available for the questions the work turns up. Review any change of method, and resist changing the question late. Delivery and sign-off: Confirm it meets the need you commissioned it for, and apply its limitations when you pass the result on. Review: Ask whether it informed the decision, whether it is still being used, and whether it should be decommissioned. Analyst. Owns the method and the write-up. Engagement and scoping: Clarify the real question and record the scope, the boundaries and the assumptions. Confirm your understanding in writing: an email is enough. Design: Choose the method, score the likelihood and read your level. Note your main assumptions: no separate assurance plan, but allow for the colleague check. Analysis: Self-check against the Level 1 checks, and keep inputs and working reproducible enough that someone else could re-run it. Delivery and sign-off: Write it up with your main limitation alongside the result and a short quality assurance statement, in an accessible format. Store the project record with it. Review: The review is yours at this level, on request or when the output changes, and at each reissue. Critical friend. A colleague, within your team. Naming the reviewer before you start is what Level 2 adds, so this lane begins at analysis. Analysis: Sense check the headline numbers against an independent reference: last period, a related series, or an order-of-magnitude expectation. Delivery and sign-off: State what you assured, and that the quality assurance was appropriate and sufficient for the level the work is at. Review: What you reported back is what the next piece of work avoids. None: This lane is empty at Engagement and scoping and Design. No separate approver. No formal sign-off beyond the analyst, so the lane is empty by design. A team lead signature is what Level 2 adds. Delivery and sign-off: Nobody signs this off at this level, so there is nothing in this lane to wait for. None: This lane is empty at Engagement and scoping, Design, Analysis and Review. What is handed over. 1: Commissioner to Analyst, at Engagement and scoping. The decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. 2: Analyst to Critical friend, at Analysis. The headline numbers, for a colleague to sense check. 3: Critical friend to Analyst, at Analysis. What the sense check found, which is the analyst's to act on. 4: Analyst to Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Draft results first, with the main limitation and a short quality assurance statement. Why this one is Level 1 Standard: The Decision row's level 1 is analysis where "no decision, action, resource allocation, policy, service or performance assessment would be materially affected", which is exploratory, informative or for learning. The Reputation row's level 1 names exploratory analysis outright. Highest impact 1 low reads Level 1 at every likelihood but very high. Level 1 is the floor, and it is still not no assurance: it is separation within your team. A colleague sense checks the headline numbers, four sections of the project record are completed, realistically one side of A4, and a short statement is required. The record is stored with the output, and the statement is not published: publishing it with the output starts at Level 3. NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.

div.b: WHY THIS ONE IS LEVEL 1 STANDARD

div.span: The Decision row's level 1 is analysis where "no decision, action, resource allocation, policy, service or performance assessment would be materially affected", which is exploratory, informative or for learning. The Reputation row's level 1 names exploratory analysis outright. Highest impact 1 low reads Level 1 at every likelihood but very high. Level 1 is the floor, and it is still not no assurance: it is separation within your team. A colleague sense checks the headline numbers, four sections of the project record are completed, realistically one side of A4, and a short statement is required. The record is stored with the output, and the statement is not published: publishing it with the output starts at Level 3.
NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.
